title: Adolescents' Homework Performance in Mathematics and Science: Personal Factors and Teaching Practices https://www.apa.org/pubs/journals/releases/edu-0000032.pdf
author: Barton, Craig
source: Tips for Teachers (tipsforteachers.co.uk), December 16, 2024 — original paper:
summary: This entry covers Fernandez-Alonso and Suarez-Alvarez's large-scale multilevel study of 7,451 Spanish adolescents, examining what actually predicts homework's contribution to math and science achievement once prior knowledge, socioeconomic status, and gender are controlled for. The strongest predictors were student autonomy in completing homework and the frequency with which teachers assigned it -- not the raw time spent or quantity assigned. The study estimates roughly one hour per day as the optimal homework duration, beyond which returns diminish. Prior academic achievement remained the single strongest overall predictor of performance, underscoring homework's role as a supporting factor rather than a primary driver. Barton draws out the practical guidance: assign homework consistently to build habits and self-directed learning, keep quantity moderate (around 60 minutes daily) but pitched at a genuinely challenging level, and encourage students to work through it independently rather than leaning on parental help, since autonomous completion was linked to better outcomes.
points: Student autonomy in completing homework and the frequency of teacher-assigned homework were stronger predictors of math/science achievement than time spent or sheer quantity.
Optimal homework duration was estimated at around one hour per day; more than that showed diminishing returns.
Working through homework independently, without parental help, was linked to better outcomes than parent-assisted completion.
Prior academic achievement remained the single strongest overall predictor, positioning homework as a supporting rather than primary driver of performance.
quotes: Our data sends a clear message to teaching professionals: well used, homework remains a vital tool for comprehensive education of adolescents. The results indicate that regular assignment of homework and how it is carried out are two key aspects
Regular homework assignments are crucial. Teachers should consistently assign homework to foster good work habits and encourage self-directed learning in students
Focus on quality over quantity. Assigning excessive amounts of homework is not effective. A reasonable and effective amount of homework is around 60 minutes per day
Promote student autonomy. Encourage students to complete their homework independently, without parental help. Students who work autonomously achieve better results
The study found that student autonomy in completing homework and the frequency of assignments by teachers were key predictors of success, more so than time spent or the quantity of homework
